html:
The Achumawi are a Native American people of northeastern California, the larger part of the Pit River people. Nine of the eleven bands of the Pit River Tribe are Achumawi; the other two are their close relatives, the Atsugewi.

They lived along the Pit River and its branches, such as the Fall River, below Mount Shasta. They fished, hunted, and gathered roots and seeds, and are known for fine basketry. The Pit River took its name from the pits they dug to trap deer.

The Gold Rush brought settlers, violence and disease to their land in the 1850s. Their neighbours included the Shasta, the Okwanuchu and the Modoc.
